algorithm.Title: Sunburn - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Sunburn severity assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for confusion, seizure, collapse, abnormal breathing, very hot skin, inability to drink, severe dehydration, or an unwell infant/child. Move to shade or air conditioning, remove excess clothing, and cool with water and airflow while following 999 instructions. Do not use ice directly or give oral fluids if drowsy, vomiting, seizing, or unsafe to swallow. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Is this a burn from direct heat, flame, hot liquid, or steam rather than sun exposure?
questions.Information: A non-solar thermal burn requires the authored Burns - Thermal pathway.

questions.Question: Was the injury caused by an acid or another chemical rather than sun exposure?
questions.Information: A chemical burn requires the authored Burns - Chemical pathway and immediate substance-specific decontamination precautions.

questions.Question: Is this an electrical or lightning injury, or is there confusion, fainting, a very high temperature with no sweating, or a rapid heartbeat suggesting heatstroke rather than simple sunburn?
questions.Information: Electrical and lightning injuries retain a conservative emergency disposition because their authored protocol is not in the generated catalog. NHS.UK also notes severe sunburn can progress to heat exhaustion and heatstroke, which needs emergency care.

questions.Question: Is the skin blistered or swollen, is the temperature very high or does the caller feel hot, cold, or shivery, does the caller feel very tired, dizzy, or sick, is there a headache or muscle cramps, or is the patient a baby or young child?
questions.Information: NHS.UK sunburn guidance lists these as reasons for an urgent clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) or the Qatar clinical-review pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) call.

questions.Question: Is this mild-to-moderate sunburn without blistering or the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes most sunburn as resolving within about a week with home care.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency heat-illness response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for confusion, seizure, collapse, abnormal breathing, very hot skin, inability to drink, severe dehydration, or an unwell infant/child. Move to shade or air conditioning, remove excess clothing, and cool with water and airflow while following 999 instructions. Do not use ice directly or give oral fluids if drowsy, vomiting, seizing, or unsafe to swallow. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening confusion or collapse; seizure or abnormal breathing; inability to drink or markedly reduced urine.

advice.Title: Urgent sunburn review
Content: Cool the skin, stay hydrated, and arrange same-day medical review, especially for blistering or a young child.
Call Back If: fever worsens; increasing dizziness.

advice.Title: Governed care for mild sunburn
Content: Leave the sun, cool skin with a cool shower or damp cloth, wear loose clothing, and maintain usual fluids if not restricted. Use only a bland unperfumed moisturiser on intact skin and do not burst blisters or apply ice. Medicine requires age, weight, pregnancy, allergy, kidney/liver disease, dehydration, and current-medicine checks.
Call Back If: large blisters, facial/eye involvement, fever, dizziness, vomiting, reduced urine, or feeling very unwell.
